1f94905d6c.q: How did a young broker transition from a corporate salary job to building a retail leasing business in Texas?
1f94905d6c.a: Tuva Patoli left her corporate job after one year to enter commercial real estate at age 22, attracted by the commission model where growth is tied directly to effort. She started with zero properties and zero tenant relationships, building her practice through consistent tenant and landlord canvassing. Today, after several years, she represents 36 shopping centers and led her team to close 95 leases in her third year in the industry.
1f94905d6c.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

9ae270e132.q: What strategies help retail brokers stand out when representing landlords in competitive markets?
9ae270e132.a: The key is to adopt a landlord's mindset before advising on deals. Rather than simply pursuing commissions, a broker should think like a property owner, evaluating which tenants genuinely fit the center's mix and refusing deals that don't make financial sense, even if commission is at stake. This approach—prioritizing the landlord's long-term interests over quick closes—builds lasting relationships and differentiates you from transactional brokers.
9ae270e132.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

86275d1ad3.q: How does retail leasing activity function as an early indicator of consumer behavior and market trends?
86275d1ad3.a: Consumer behavior changes fast and can be observed month-by-month through retail leasing activity in real time. What tenants are leasing reflects the actual trends happening in the market—the backbone of broader economic shifts. During COVID, for example, essential retail like pizza shops, taco shops, and nail salons remained active, while large national brands closed, showing how leasing directly mirrors shifting consumer needs.
86275d1ad3.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

71fa62bbb3.q: What role does tenant canvassing play in building a retail leasing practice from scratch?
71fa62bbb3.a: Tenant canvassing is recommended as the starting point for new brokers. When canvassing tenants, the broker is the expert teaching them about market conditions, rental rates, and which submarkets are suitable for their business. This is different from landlord canvassing, which is harder because landlords already possess expertise. Canvassing requires consistent effort—putting hundreds of miles on your car, meeting owners in person, obtaining direct contact information, and being persistently but respectfully pushy.
71fa62bbb3.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

00be8a2852.q: How can excessive pressure from one party in a real estate negotiation compromise the deal?
00be8a2852.a: When brokers relay landlord pressure directly to tenants, it can damage relationships and kill deals. Early in her career, Tuva transmitted a landlord's urgency to a hot chicken restaurant owner during lease execution, causing the tenant to question the property and threaten to walk away. A senior mentor intervened to calm the tenant, teaching her that regardless of pressure from one side, the other party needs time for due diligence, attorney review, and red-lining. Never translate external pressure onto the client.
00be8a2852.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

6cae7ea4f6.q: How has a retail specialist's daily responsibilities evolved from entry-level leasing to managing a team?
6cae7ea4f6.a: Daily work centers on consistency across the Texas market, primarily in Houston and Dallas, split roughly 75% landlord representation and 25% tenant representation. Tasks range from lease negotiation and tenant communication to property site visits—sometimes driving 45 minutes to investigate operational issues. Every day presents different challenges; there is no fixed daily routine. With a team, work scales by delegation: while one person negotiates with a tenant, another manages landlord relationships, multiplying deal velocity.
6cae7ea4f6.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

edde16a269.q: What volume metrics define a high-performing year in third-party retail leasing?
edde16a269.a: In her third year in commercial real estate, Tuva's leasing team (three people total: herself, a vice president of leasing, and one associate) closed approximately 95 leases across 36 represented shopping centers, averaging roughly two to three tenants per center annually. She notes this figure represents team output—no individual can sustain 95 leases alone—and she is now focused on 2026 volume goals rather than reviewing past performance.
edde16a269.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

310197c038.q: How does real-world prospecting and market knowledge drive deal execution in retail leasing?
310197c038.a: Early in her career, Tuva prospected extensively for a 3,000 square foot Houston location suitable for a second-generation restaurant concept. Using her deep knowledge of the neighborhood and scanning local social media for trending food concepts, she identified and contacted a hot chicken restaurant owner directly. Although the initial deal faced complications due to communication pressure, the foundational prospecting and tenant relationship ultimately resulted in successful lease execution and a repeat transaction years later.
310197c038.e: The Broker Who Thinks Like a Landlord: Inside Texas Retail Leasing with Tooba Patoli

bb9569371d.q: How did Justin Kazana transition from sports broadcasting at Fox Sportsnet to commercial real estate in Knoxville?
bb9569371d.a: Justin worked in television and radio sports broadcasting for nearly 10 years, including roles at Fox Sportsnet and Comcast Sports doing play-by-play for SEC football championships and Olympic sports. However, he decided to transition back to the family business around 2004 when he realized the broadcasting hours and travel schedule conflicted with raising a family, as sports do not take place nine to five Monday through Friday. He returned to Knoxville and worked with his father for six years in property management and development before opening the Cushman & Wakefield office.
bb9569371d.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

b53eb35679.q: When did the Cushman & Wakefield Knoxville office open and how many brokers started on the first day?
b53eb35679.a: The Cushman & Wakefield office in Knoxville opened in 2010 with seven brokers on the first day, all of them experienced deal-makers. The office has since grown to 25 brokers and now manages almost three million square feet of space around the market while doing some of the biggest deals in Knoxville.
b53eb35679.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

b4b175eb3c.q: Why did the Knoxville Avis & Young office migrate from Cushman & Wakefield in 2015?
b4b175eb3c.a: The decision to migrate from Cushman & Wakefield to Avis & Young in 2015 was driven by Cushman's acquisition by DTZ. The Knoxville office wanted to maintain local ownership and favorable commission splits that work for a tertiary market like Knoxville, rather than being required to meet Cushman's national commission splits that would have caused them to lose brokers. About 84 people made the transition across the Knoxville, Nashville, and Memphis offices to Avis & Young.
b4b175eb3c.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

7f874b6dc2.q: What is the key to maintaining leadership in secondary and tertiary commercial real estate markets like Knoxville?
7f874b6dc2.a: Success in markets like Knoxville depends on becoming a thought leader and industry leader involved day to day in community activities such as city council committees, chamber of commerce boards, and boards of realtors. Relationships are paramount because you are working as a trusted advisor managing not just transactions but long-term relationships, and in smaller markets you will cross paths repeatedly—at dinner, Little League games, or community events—making it critical never to burn bridges.
7f874b6dc2.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

97b048a973.q: How did Justin Kazana structure his team and staffing to scale the Avis & Young Knoxville office beyond brokerage only?
97b048a973.a: Justin hired a COO four years ago who did not have a real estate background but could operate the office, manage property management operations, negotiate IT contracts, and handle insurance and tech support. He also hired assistants and a virtual assistant in the last 18 months to handle marketing, lease amendments, and administrative work. This allowed him to focus on deals rather than operations, and he credits the book '10X is Easier Than 2X' by Dan Sullivan for helping him identify the 20 percent of tasks he should keep and delegate the other 80 percent.
97b048a973.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

804d76bdad.q: What specific construction and development experience did Justin Kazana gain working with his father before opening the Cushman & Wakefield office?
804d76bdad.a: Working with his father for six years, Justin managed leasing and marketing of a significant office portfolio, one industrial building, and two retail buildings. His company was building an office building approximately every 18 months, each about 50,000 square feet, on an 80-acre office development off Pellissippi Parkway between the airport, Knoxville, and Oak Ridge National Labs. This hands-on experience with grading contracts, construction projects, and development taught him the real costs and complexities involved in real estate, such as the full expense of moving a wall two feet versus moving it forty feet—they are the same.
804d76bdad.e: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets
